cases.title: Disability Intergroup Reviews Key Disability Rights Priorities
cases.disability_relevance: Disability-rights advocacy and implementation priorities raised by the European Parliament Disability Intergroup.
evidence: Intergroup members called for stronger implementation of disability rights and discussed the Enhanced Disability Rights Strategy.
The meeting considered housing, artificial intelligence and the EU simplification agenda as issues affecting disabled people.
An EDF update identified the next EU budget and Digital Networks Act as priorities for joint work with the disability movement.

cases.title: Will the House of Lords improve accessibility in the Railways Bill?
cases.disability_relevance: The article examines proposed rail legislation and its effect on disabled passengers' access and legal rights.
evidence: The Railways Bill was before the House of Lords, where amendments could improve how railways operate for disabled passengers.
The Bill creates Great British Railways and other public bodies responsible for shaping the future rail network.
House of Commons proposals for stronger legal rights were not adopted; a government factsheet instead describes an accessibility duty and consideration of disabled passengers' needs.

cases.title: BCA calls for calm in smart glasses ban debate
cases.disability_relevance: Blind and partially sighted people use smart glasses as assistive technology and reported safety concerns about hostile public debate.
evidence: Blind Citizens Australia warned that calls to ban smart glasses were putting blind and partially sighted people in danger.
The organisation described smart glasses as assistive technology that can combine several platforms in one wearable device.
Members and other users reported feeling unsafe using the devices in public, while some councils had introduced ad hoc bans at facilities.
